title: Telugu Horror Film 418 Opens at Rs 2.65 Crore, Fifth-Biggest Post-COVID Start for the Genre
excerpt: Prashant Neel-presented, Mythri-backed 418 beat its low buzz with a Rs 3.13 crore gross opening day; word of mouth now decides its run.
body:
• The Telugu horror film 418 opened with Rs 2.65 crore net (Rs 3.13 crore gross) in India on Friday, October 23, despite limited pre-release buzz.
  • That is the fifth-biggest opening for a Telugu horror film in the post-COVID era, behind The RajaSaab, Virupaksha, Korean Kanakaraju and Mangalavaaram.
  • Presented by Prashant Neel and backed by Mythri Movie Makers, the film marks director Kirtan Nadagouda's debut and stars Chaithra J. Achar.
  • Its run now depends on word of mouth: reviews are mixed to positive, and the Saturday-Sunday numbers will decide whether the strong start holds.

The Telugu-language horror thriller 418 has opened well above what its quiet promotional campaign predicted, earning Rs 2.65 crore net in India on its first day, October 23 — a gross of Rs 3.13 crore — according to Koimoi.

The film is set in a medical college in a remote village, where a building's Room No. 418 has stayed sealed for 15 years. An 18-year-old medical student, Vivek Shankar, is allotted Room 417 next door and begins experiencing supernatural phenomena as he tries to uncover what lies behind the locked door. It is written and directed by debutant Kirtan Nadagouda and stars Chaithra J. Achar, Surya Raj Veerabathini and Charan Lakkaraju.

"Just behind 418 sit Rakasa at Rs 2.6 crore and Maa Oori Polimera 2 at Rs 2.35 crore."

Top five among post-COVID Telugu horror openings

With Rs 2.65 crore, 418 records the fifth-biggest opening day for a Telugu horror film since COVID, Koimoi's chart shows: The RajaSaab (2026) leads at Rs 53.73 crore, followed by Virupaksha (2023) at Rs 7.4 crore, Korean Kanakaraju (2026) at Rs 3.95 crore and Mangalavaaram (2023) at Rs 2.75 crore. Just behind 418 sit Rakasa at Rs 2.6 crore and Maa Oori Polimera 2 at Rs 2.35 crore. Earlier genre benchmarks were far smaller — Zombie Reddy opened at Rs 1.51 crore in 2021, Masooda at Rs 63 lakh in 2022 and Pindam at Rs 40 lakh in 2023 — which underlines how much the market for Telugu horror has grown.

https://x.com/MythriOfficial/status/2113553581961797785

Zoom TV reported the same Rs 2.65 crore net and Rs 3.13 crore gross figures, and Sacnilk's day-one tracker independently lists Rs 2.65 crore net for the film, which runs 2 hours 28 minutes and carries an A certificate.

Neel's name, Mythri's backing

Two names did the marketing work the campaign did not. The film is presented by Prashant Neel, the KGF director, and backed by Mythri Movie Makers, one of Telugu cinema's biggest production houses. For a debut director and a cast without a marquee star, that combination gave exhibitors and audiences a reason to take the opening seriously. Dinesh Divakaran handled cinematography and Venky GG composed the music.

What decides its fate now

Opening-day numbers buy a horror film a weekend, not a verdict. Reviews have been mixed to positive — our earlier coverage noted critics praising Chaithra Achar's performance in a promising but flawed horror tale — and both Koimoi and Zoom stress that sustained word of mouth over Saturday and Sunday will determine whether 418 converts a top-five opening into a profitable run. Advance bookings tracked by Sacnilk for the days ahead will give the first signal.
